subject: Post-demo clarifications — data routing, residency, logs and DPA next steps
messages:
From: Amira Patel <amira.patel@stellarhealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-12T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifications after today's demo — DPA scoping, logs & residency

Hi Lauren / team,

Thanks for the demo this morning — it was helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams as we scope the pilot:

- Controller vs processor: we need an explicit mapping for the flow that touches patient PII (which fields are considered PII by Redwood and which processing steps you consider controller-led vs customer-led).
- Subprocessors: can you share an up-to-date list and confirm whether any third parties will have access to raw request payloads?
- Breach/notice timing: our legal team asks if Redwood commits to contractually notify us within 48 hours of a subprocessor event that materially affects data.
- Logging & retention: default audit log retention, ability to shorten retention or purge PII on demand, and the level of detail captured (IP, prompt text, response text, token-level traces).
- Data residency: we need to understand the exact regions available for residency (EU, US, APAC) and whether model inference ever leaves the selected region for fallback.

We attached a short list of questions the legal team put together and a redline of our preferred DPA clauses (attached to this message).

Can we get a written response to these items and a follow-up call with your privacy engineer (if possible) tomorrow? Procurement will likely request SOC 2 evidence once scoping is aligned.

Thanks,
Amira Patel
Sr. Security & Risk
StellarHealth

Attachments: Stellar_DPA_questions.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document); Stellar_DPA_redline.pdf (application/pdf)

Subject: Re: Clarifications after today's demo — technical breakdown

Amira — quick technical breakdown below. I've kept the answers concise and flagged items we recommend moving into contract language. Happy to go deeper on the call.

1) Controller vs Processor mapping
- High level: StellarHealth is the controller for patient-identifiable inputs (you determine lawful basis and purposes). Redwood acts as a processor when hosting and performing model inference on your behalf.
- Exceptions: When Redwood ingests telemetry for platform reliability (metric aggregates), we process as a subprocessor for platform ops — we do not use raw prompt/response data for model training.
- Recommended clause: explicit statement that Redwood will not use customer prompts/responses for model training without opt-in.

2) Subprocessors & access to payloads
- Current subprocessors: listed at https://www.redwood.ai/subprocessors (we keep this page updated).
- Who sees raw payloads: only Redwood infra nodes in the inference path may have access; subcontractors only see encrypted storage unless explicitly provisioned.
- If you need per-processor evidence (SOC2 reports), we can provide a package under NDA.

3) Breach / notification timing
- Operational practice: initial notification within 48 hours for incidents with suspected customer data impact (we provide a triage summary).
- Confirmed incident timeline: a full incident report with root cause analysis and remediation plan within 72 hours after confirmation.
- Contract ask: Redwood is willing to commit to a 72-hour confirmed-report SLA; for 48-hour preliminary notifications we will include a best-effort clause and rapid triage. If Stellar requires 48-hour contractual guarantee for preliminary notifications, that is escalable under an enterprise SLA (we should document in the DPA/Exhibit).

4) Logging & retention
- Default: operational audit logs (metadata only — timestamps, request IDs, model used, latency, token counts) retained for 30 days; customer-configurable audit exports available.
- PII in logs: prompt and response text are not retained by default for hosted inference unless you enable full-request logging. If full-request logging is enabled we store request/response for the configured retention window.
- Purge options: API endpoints to purge retained data within a 24–48 hour window once a verified purge request is received (time varies by storage tier).
- Longer retention: 90/365-day retention options available as a paid add-on with additional access controls and encryption-at-rest key management.

5) Data residency & routing
- Residency options: US (us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1), APAC (ap-southeast-1).
- Fallback behavior: by default we will not route inference outside the selected residency. Automatic fallbacks to other regions only happen under capacity outages and will be explicitly documented in the fallback policy; we can disable cross-region fallback for regulated workloads.

Attachments included for this thread: Redwood_DPA_v2_redline.pdf; subprocessors_matrix_v1.csv.

Proposed next steps:
- I can join the call tomorrow at 2pm PT for the technical walkthrough.
- If Stellar needs a binding 48-hour preliminary notification commitment we should surface that to our commercial team so we can scope SLA pricing and operational verification.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Privacy & Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

Thanks all — that is very helpful and answers most of the team's initial questions. A few items we need to confirm before we can move to procurement: 

1) Can Redwood provide a SOC 2 package and, if needed, per-subprocessor attestations under NDA? Procurement will require this before the pilot start.
2) We need explicit contract language guaranteeing a 48-hour preliminary notification for subprocessor events that reasonably appear to impact Stellar data. We understand confirmed-root-cause in 72 hours is common; the 48-hour preliminary timeline needs to be in the DPA. If that's not standard, please identify the commercial/ops path to get this committed.
3) Please confirm the API endpoint and expected SLA for data purge requests (24–48 hours is acceptable, please confirm the worst-case SLA).

If you can push a short addendum (bullet-pointed) that we can share with procurement today, that would speed things up. We are targeting a pilot kickoff in early December.

I'll block 2pm PT for the call — Tom and I will be on.

Best,
Amira Patel
Sr. Security & Risk | StellarHealth
amira.patel@stellarhealth.com
